10. Worked Example
The example below directly demonstrates a simplified DPO-style loss, already covered in this topic, computed directly from preference pairs.

code.content:
import math

def log_prob(response_score):
    # already covered as directly optimizing on preference pairs in this topic
    return math.log(response_score)

def dpo_loss(preferred_prob, rejected_prob, beta=1.0):
    # already covered as a closed form loss function in this topic
    logit = beta * (log_prob(preferred_prob) - log_prob(rejected_prob))
    probability_preferred_is_better = 1 / (1 + math.exp(-logit))
    loss = -math.log(probability_preferred_is_better)
    return loss

# already covered as collecting human preference data in RLHF
preference_pairs = [
    {"preferred_prob": 0.8, "rejected_prob": 0.3},
    {"preferred_prob": 0.6, "rejected_prob": 0.55},
]

print("DPO loss per preference pair (already covered in this topic):")
for pair in preference_pairs:
    loss = dpo_loss(pair["preferred_prob"], pair["rejected_prob"])
    print(f"  preferred={pair['preferred_prob']}, rejected={pair['rejected_prob']} -> loss={loss:.4f}")

# already covered as only one model to train in this topic
print("\nNote: this loss trains the single policy model directly, with no separate reward model involved")
